chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man departed from Arafat, passed by Al-Mash'ar, but did not stand (pause) until he reached Mina, and threw the Jamarah, and he was unaware until the day rose. He (peace be upon him) said: He should return to Al-Mash'ar and stand there, then return and throw the Jamarah.

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ: Al-Mash'ar (Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram), the second major station of Hajj
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the primary station of Hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the third major station of Hajj
key_terms.يَقِفْ: To stand/pause (wuquf), a ritual act of standing at a station

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the pause at Al-Mash'ar and proceeds directly to Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the compensatory ritual (qada) for a pilgrim who missed the mandatory standing at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram due to ignorance or delay, a key detail in Shia fiqh regarding the sequence of Hajj rites. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs that the pilgrim must return to Al-Mash'ar to perform the missed wuquf before proceeding to Mina to throw the Jamarah, ensuring the ritual order is rectified. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the precise chronological order of Hajj pillars, distinguishing it from other schools where the standing at Mash'ar may be considered less critical if missed unintentionally.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man departs from Arafaat, so he passed by the ‘الْمَشْعَرِ’ Monuments, but he does not paused until he ends up to Mina and pelts the Jamarah, and he does not know until the day is raised’. Heasws said: ‘He should return to the ‘الْمَشْعَرِ’ Monuments, so he should pause at it, then he should return, so he would pelt the Jamarah’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“Once, I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who leaves ‘Arafat and passes through al-Mash‘ar to Mina 5 without staying in al-Mash‘ar. In Mina’he throws pebbles on al-Jamarat and only when the sun rises high he comes to know. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must go back to al-Mash‘ar, stay there for a while, then return to Mina 5 and throw pebbles . ‘“
